title: ArchSync: Evidence-Backed Conformance Checking for TypeScript Service Architectures
abstract: Passing tests do not establish that a service change conforms to its intended architecture. ArchSync links a machine-readable architectural contract to selected HTTP, PostgreSQL, Redis and AMQP observations in TypeScript, retains source evidence, and maps introduced findings to PASS, BLOCK or REVIEW at a Git change. We evaluate this deterministic prototype using co-developed development datasets: 20 isolated architecture patches, 40 annotated detector signals, and an incremental replay of those same patches. A separately reported hardening campaign checks a finite rule domain against a matrix oracle and exercises adversarial source and cache behavior. The controlled observations support contract coherence and regression reliability. They do not establish representative accuracy, comparative superiority or developer productivity; independently labeled repositories and a capability-matched external comparison remain necessary. The contribution is an auditable integration of service-level observations, explicit rules and change-time decisions, together with evidence that exposes its reliability boundaries.
